=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- CLAUDE.md:476-558; unattended_system_instructions.md:377-456 | flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The PR adds the automation-bias policy text in §18/§20, but the reviewer says the same content was already merged via PR #2746 / commit 5342173.
  WHY: The branch is duplicating content already present in origin/main, so the change is redundant.
- CLAUDE.md:492 | confidence=2 | flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `**STOP and ask**` in §18.A tells the interactive Claude agent to stop before adding a manual-invocation script, while the unattended policy says to surface it explicitly in the plan output instead.
  WHY: The reviewer explicitly called this an intentional interactive/unattended split rather than a defect.
- CLAUDE.md:531-535 | confidence=4 | flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: §18.D cites `§10.E` / `§10.C` even though the referenced MongoDB rules are organized as unlabeled bullets, so the cross-reference text does not match the document structure.
  WHY: One reviewer flagged the non-existent subsection labels and another flagged the `§10` vs `§12` mismatch; both point to the same inconsistent cross-reference text.
- CLAUDE.md:543-558 | confidence=4 | flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new policy says plans omitting required wiring/gate details `MUST` be revised, but no validator, template update, or reviewer checklist entry enforces that requirement.
  WHY: Without machine-readable enforcement, incomplete plans can still pass review and reach implementation.
- unattended_system_instructions.md:442-456 | confidence=5 | flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: §20.E requires a dedicated top-of-plan checklist for scheduler wiring, supervisor needs, and DB gate patterns, but nothing in the workflow enforces or parses it.
  WHY: The reviewer says orchestrator runs can still accept plans that omit the checklist, so the policy is not operational.
- unattended_system_instructions.md:385-456 | confidence=4 | flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new §20.A/§20.E combination creates a self-contradictory edge case when these policy files themselves are updated, because the producing plan would also have to satisfy the policy it is adding.
  WHY: The reviewer says future runs touching these policy files can violate the newly added rules and stall the review flow.
- CLAUDE.md:476 | confidence=5 | flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Inserting §18 before FINAL REMINDER shifts the top-level numbering/layout and breaks the reviewer's backward-compatibility expectations.
  WHY: The reviewer says downstream consumers that grep section headings or rely on the old layout can load mismatched context.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
